title: THE THUMOO-S TEST
about: The Governor hires a podcast philosopher to test his livestock for courage; the cow passes, the state certifies it Silver class, and Big Don learns that a citizen cannot be dinner.

beats.text: A Texas ranch at midday. The Governor has bought a book about Plato, and now he must find out which of his citizens have courage.
see: a man in a cowboy hat leaning on a fence

beats.text: Now, Bro-crates, I invited you out here because you said you could help me identify the spirited citizens.
Oh, absolutely. Thumos. The courage gland. We're gonna Socratically interrogate this cow.
Asking questions of a creature that cannot answer is an old method. In ancient Athens, they say, Socrates tried it on a goat.
see: an old marble statue of a bearded man

beats.text: Tell me, goat, what is virtue?
Maaaaa.
Ah. You admit you do not know. Excellent.
Okay. First question. Cow... what is courage? Is courage... the willingness to face danger? Would you say you face danger... every day... by existing near a grill?
Bro-crates, we don't threaten the livestock with barbecue.
Moo.
WHOA. That's basically an admission of fearlessness.
That sounded like a moo.
Exactly. The moo is a refusal to elaborate. That's pure alpha energy.
A Board of Regents machine flies in over the fence with a form. A cow that shows courage can be certified Silver class, a guardian of the state.
see: a small airplane flying low over a field
a man filling in a form

beats.text: Well I'll be. We can make a cow a Guardian?
Dude... imagine. A cow with civic virtue. A cow that protects the ranch.
Now hold on. If the cow becomes Silver-class, does it still get to be... eaten?
That is... the real Allegory of the Cave.
'Cause I'm not gonna lie, I got plans for that cow.
MOO.
See?! Defiance! That's thumos! That's courage! That cow just refused your culinary authoritarianism!

beats.ask: you can't argue with a cow

beats.text: The verdict comes back. The cow displays courage. It is Silver class now, and in this Republic the Silver class cannot be owned.
see: a rubber stamp on a document
a cow standing in a field

beats.text: Congratulations, Don. You just liberated your own brisket.
...So the cow is... emancipated.
Through a gate nobody remembers opening, the cow walks off toward the horizon, calm and free.
see: a cow walking through an open gate

beats.text: That's a citizen right there.
Well... good luck. And if you see my feed bucket, tell it to come home!
